priceSnapshot.note: Morning asked for a post-CPI confirmation close above 64,300 and the tape delivered the exact opposite. July CPI printed at 12:30Z dead in line with consensus - headline +0.1% m/m and 3.4% y/y, core +0.2% m/m and 2.5% y/y, all three matching the Dow Jones estimate and all three a tenth cooler than June. Equities took it as a green light: QQQ is +0.95% at 725.25 and VOO +0.37% at 711.01, both printing 21-day highs while this report is written. BTC did the reverse. The 12:00Z 1H bar spiked to 64,496.9 within two minutes of the release, tagging 197 points above morning's add line, and then closed 64,125.9 - the entire spike given back inside the same hour. The 13:00Z bar closed 63,841.6, the 14:00Z bar closed 63,370.2 after trading down to 63,366.6, and price has spent the four hours since grinding a 63,318.9-63,580.0 range. The damage is structural, not cosmetic. The 4H bar that opened 12:00Z settled 63,445.9, which is 290.9 points BELOW the 4H EMA200 at 63,736.84 - the reclaim that midnight and morning both built their case on survived exactly two settles and then failed on the third. Morning's own reduce line at 63,700 has now been broken by four consecutive settled 1H closes: 63,841.6 was the last one above, then 63,370.2, 63,445.9, 63,492.3 and 63,475.2. That is not the sweep this desk warned itself about two sessions ago; a sweep reclaims, and four hours of basing 255 points underneath the line is a settled rejection. The positioning is the part that should worry a long. Realized long liquidations over the trailing 23 hours are $2,437,558 against $1,391,172 of shorts, so the flush was paid for by longs this time. And yet the OKX long/short account ratio has gone the WRONG way - 1.68 at the morning read, 1.83 now - while open interest rose 1.15% to $2,086,233,942 and funding went from +0.00384% to +0.01000% per 8h. Retail added longs into a failed reclaim, on rising open interest, with funding turning back positive. That is the setup that produces the next leg down, and it is the single most important thing that changed since 07:00.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close below $63,237.6 - the two-day low and the floor of the current base. This is the SECOND reduce of the day; the first, morning's 63,700 line, has already fired on four consecutive settled closes and is being honoured in this session with a 25% spot trim. The next line is placed at the low rather than inside the 63,400 shelf ($473,618) deliberately, applying the lesson this desk wrote into its own ledger on 11 August: a reduce line sitting INSIDE an unconsumed liquidity shelf measures a stop hunt, not a trend, and 63,400 is exactly such a shelf and is only 45 points from spot. 63,237.6 sits BELOW the whole cluster band, so a settled close through it is price leaving the zone rather than price hunting it. Only $215,856 of realized-liquidation mass sits between 63,200 and 63,300, so a break there has very little to absorb it.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close above $63,900 with aggregate open interest NOT rising across the same bar. The price line is 455 points above spot because a smaller number buys nothing: 63,900 is the first level that puts price back above the 4H EMA200 at 63,736.84 with room to spare AND clears the 1H EMA20 at 63,762.97, and it sits on top of the $329,783 shelf rather than under it. The open-interest condition is the same inversion endday wrote on 11 August and it has now filtered correctly twice - it rejected the 09:00Z bar this morning and passed the 10:00Z bar. Its job today is to refuse a bounce funded by the same crowd that just pushed the long/short account ratio to 1.83.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from ADD to REDUCE, and this is the reverse of this morning firing exactly as written. Morning published reduceIf 63,700 on TWO settled 1H closes below, with the confirmation deliberately widened so a single CPI whipsaw would not trigger it. Four closes have now printed below - 63,370.2, 63,445.9, 63,492.3 and 63,475.2 - across more than four hours, with no reclaim attempt reaching even 63,600. The trigger is not merely satisfied, it is satisfied with margin, and the thesis it was written to protect (the 4H EMA200 reclaim) is broken on the 12:00Z settle. So the wallet trims 25% of the spot core here, raising cash from 33.89 to roughly 74 USDT. The trim is partial, not a flatten, for three reasons that all argue against panic: the downside liquidation map is genuinely thin, $689,474 across 63,400/63,300/63,200 versus $3,139,255 stacked above spot; the 15m MACD histogram has turned positive at +3.80 for the first time since the flush began; and price has held a 261-point base for four hours instead of extending. The resting stop is reset from morning's 63,480 - which is now ABOVE spot and meaningless - down to 63,180, just beneath the 63,237.6 two-day low and the $110,223 shelf at 63,200. Futures stay flat. There is no leverage case in a 261-point range with the fast chart turning up underneath a broken 4H average; expressing the stance in spot is the honest version of it.

liquidityMagnet.note: $3,139,255 of realized-liquidation mass sits ABOVE spot against $689,474 below, so on cluster weight alone the pull is up and the nearest magnet is the $524,502 shelf at 63,600, only 155 points away. That reading needs an honest caveat. These are REALIZED fills, not resting orders - the mass above spot is where longs were force-sold on the way down from 64,496.9, so it marks consumed liquidity and overhead supply as much as it marks attraction. The more actionable half of the same data is the thin band underneath: only $689,474 of forced selling has printed below 63,445 across 23 hours, which means a breakdown would have very little cascade fuel to feed on. Both readings point the same way for sizing - trim, do not flatten.

The EMA stack is bearish and complete - price is 318.0 points under the EMA20, 531.1 under the EMA50, 705.5 under the EMA200 and 763.2 under the EMA100 - and every one of those averages is now overhead resistance rather than support. timeframes.structure: The decisive chart, and it has revoked its own answer. Midnight framed the whole day as a coin balanced on the EMA200 at 63,742.93; morning reported two consecutive settles above it - 63,833.3 then 64,236.3 - and called the reclaim extended rather than merely defended. The third settle killed it. The 12:00Z bar opened 64,236.3, spiked to 64,496.9 on the CPI print, and closed 63,445.9, which is 290.9 points BELOW the EMA200 at 63,736.84. A 1,051-point range that opens above an average, tags a new high and closes below it is a bearish outside bar, and it is the single most reliable pattern on this chart. The MACD had narrowed from -154.96 to -127.94 across the recovery; it has widened back out to -70.84 with the line at -253.66, so the momentum repair is fully reversed. Price is now 709.3 points below the EMA20, 795.1 below the EMA100 and 852.0 below the EMA200's nearest neighbour at EMA50 64,296.96. ATR(14) is 477.27, so the whole 261-point base fits inside 0.55 of one average bar - this range is small enough that it resolves rather than persists.

calibration.note: Morning's ADD is marked a clear miss. It executed 15 USDT of spot at 64,233.8 and price is 63,445.0, so the tranche is -788.8 points or -1.23%, roughly -$0.18 on the notional. The process defence is real but partial: the add trigger endday wrote (settled 1H close above 63,930 with open interest falling across the bar) fired correctly and the open-interest inversion did filter the 09:00Z bar out, which is exactly what it was built for. What the trigger could not see was that it was firing thirty minutes before a scheduled macro release into a 15m RSI of 72.41. The transferable point is that a mechanical trigger has no clock: it fired on a valid bar, but the bar sat inside an event window that the desk had itself identified in writing two sessions earlier and then chose to trade in front of anyway. Morning's reduce line at 63,700 was the better half of that report and it has now fired with margin. Both of morning's published lines therefore resolved within six hours - the add into a loss, the reduce into a correct exit signal - which is the same double-fire pattern the 11 August midday session produced and wrote a lesson about.
